cds.text: Identify and compare attributes of objects and events (length, capacity, mass, duration) using direct comparison and explain reasoning
Compare directly and indirectly, and order objects and events by length, mass, capacity and duration, explaining reasoning
Measure and compare objects by length, capacity and mass using uniform informal units, and smaller units when more accuracy is needed
Identify which metric units measure everyday items; use known measurements to make estimates
Interpret unmarked and partial units when measuring length, mass, capacity, duration and temperature, using scaled and digital instruments
Choose appropriate metric units for length, mass and capacity; use smaller units or combined units for greater accuracy
Convert between common metric units of length, mass and capacity; use decimal metric measurements suited to the problem's context
Sequence days of the week and times of day and link them to familiar events
Measure lengths of shapes and objects with informal units that are uniform and placed end-to-end
Identify common uses of halves, quarters and eighths with shapes, objects and events, and represent them
Measure and compare objects using familiar metric units of length, mass and capacity, and instruments with labelled markings
Recognise ways to measure and approximate perimeter and area of shapes and enclosed spaces using formal and informal units
Solve practical problems involving perimeter and area of regular and irregular shapes using appropriate metric units
Establish the formula for the area of a rectangle and use it to solve practical problems
Describe the duration and sequence of events using years, months, weeks, days and hours
Identify dates and find the number of days between events using calendars
Use the relationship between formal time units (days, hours, minutes, seconds) to estimate and compare event durations
Solve problems involving duration, including am and pm situations and conversions between time units
Compare 12-hour and 24-hour time systems and solve practical problems converting between them
Interpret and use timetables and itineraries to plan activities and find durations of events and journeys
Recognise and read time on an analog clock to the hour, half-hour and quarter-hour
Describe the relationship between hours and minutes on analog and digital clocks; read time to the nearest minute
Estimate and compare angles using names (acute, obtuse, straight, reflex, revolution) and relate them to a right angle
Estimate, construct and measure angles in degrees with a protractor; relate measures to angle names
Identify relationships between angles on a straight line, angles at a point and vertically opposite angles; use them to find unknown angles and explain reasoning
Identify, describe and show quarter, half, three-quarter and full turns in everyday situations
Identify angles as measures of turn and compare them with right angles in everyday situations
Recognise relationships between dollars and cents and represent money values in different ways
